| R-01 | defect | MAJOR | packet severity HIGH — contract-test gap on the i6 seam. The turn_start reassertion (index.ts:523-533) and the session-generation cancellation (index.ts:540-541, plus the four generation guards at :178, :182, :186, :188, :191) have ZERO test coverage. CLAIM: `grep -rn turn_start .pi/extensions/pij --include='*.test.ts'` returns only core/receipts.test.ts, core/session.test.ts and core/harness/copilot.test.ts — all of which exercise PijSession.onTurnStart, never the index.ts `pi.on("turn_start", ...)` handler; index.test.ts contains no occurrence of `turn_start` at all and never invokes handlers.get("turn_start"). PROOF: the phase execution log (assets/tasks/phase-1/execution.log.md) asserts both behaviours as delivered — 'first turn schedules one extra attempt after startup failure' and 'stale session generations cannot overwrite a replacement session' — with `index.test.ts: 13/13 pass` as the receipt, but none of those 13 touch either behaviour. Both are therefore claims, not witnesses, and are one refactor away from silent deletion. SMALLEST FIX: two wiring tests in index.test.ts using the existing makeFakePi/handlers harness — (a) omp session_start with a setSessionName that never lands, then `handlers.get("turn_start")`, assert exactly one additional setSessionName after the publication settles; (b) omp session_start, then session_shutdown, then assert a late setSessionName/setStatus from the stale publication is dropped. | .pi/extensions/pij/index.ts:523-533,540-541 | — | — | — | — | — | — |

Extension loading order is precisely the mechanism whose timing the race turns on, so `--no-extensions -e &lt;path&gt;` changes the independent variable. Recommended AC1 note: 'second surface guaranteed by construction; native-segment rate improved but not separated at n=10'. | — | — | — | — |
| R-03 | defect | MINOR | packet severity MEDIUM — G3's honest-failure notice can be a false claim. publishSeatName emits `pij: could not set omp session name — id is &lt;self&gt;` as the last statement of the bounded window; the turn_start reassertion is chained onto that same promise (`void publication.result.then(...)`), so the extra attempt runs strictly AFTER the notice has already been rendered by ctx.ui.notify(..., 'warning'). If the reassertion then succeeds, the operator is left with a standing warning that is now untrue, and nothing retracts it. Compounding: the reassertion's result is discarded — `publication.result` is reassigned at index.ts:529 and never read — so a successful reassertion is unobservable to the extension, and `noticeShown` latching means no corrected notice is possible either. SMALLEST FIX: give publishSeatName a caller-supplied final-attempt hook, or move the notice out of the helper's tail into index.ts so it is emitted only after the one reassertion has had its chance (and skipped if that reassertion takes). | .pi/extensions/pij/core/session-name.ts:41 + .pi/extensions/pij/index.ts:527-530 | — | — | — | — | — | — |

When `getSessionName` is absent, publishSeatName can never return took:true: it exhausts the whole schedule and emits the honest-failure notice even when every single setSessionName call SUCCEEDED. SMALLEST FIX: in blind mode return took as unknown-or-true-on-no-throw and suppress the notice (a blind publisher has no grounds to claim it could not set the name), and rename the test to say what it now asserts. | .pi/extensions/pij/core/session-name.ts:34-41 and .pi/extensions/pij/core/session-name.test.ts:86-108 | — | — | — | — | — | — |

Non-omp rs renders `${self} · rs-v1` in the keyed row; omp+rs now renders bare `self`, because the helper hardcodes the row text to `self` (session-name.ts:18).
